_comment: The comment-density ratchet (#861). Doctrine governs what a comment may say; this budget governs how much. The metric is CHARACTER SHARE — non-whitespace characters inside TypeScript-parser comment ranges over non-whitespace characters of the whole file — measured by scripts/check-comment-density-ratchet.mjs over every git-tracked packages/** and apps/** .ts/.tsx file except .d.ts. Characters, not lines: a line count is gamed by fusing three comment lines into one wrapped sentence, and holding whitespace out of both sides keeps blank lines and reflowing out of the number. Every measured file carries a pin [commentChars, totalChars] and enforcement is DOWN-ONLY: any rise in a pinned file's share fails the gate, compared by integer cross-multiplication so a re-pin is exact and no regression rounds into the noise. Downward re-pins are free — `node scripts/check-comment-density-ratchet.mjs --write` recomputes every pin, adds new files, prunes deleted ones, and refuses to raise a pin, so --write cannot launder a regression. A deliberate raise is a hand edit to this file carrying an approved-deviation note in the issue receipt. A file with no pin and at least 40 non-blank lines fails above a 15% share; the global target is <=10% and the gate prints the running figure on every run, pass or fail. `allowlist` exempts a named file from the 15% cap ONLY, never from its pin, for registries where the prose IS the payload — it is the pressure valve that exists so nobody deletes load-bearing rationale to hit a number.
approvedDeviation: #890 hand-raises 66 pins the --write refuses to move. Two causes, kept apart on purpose. 48 of them are on files this branch changed: the mobile testing rebuild's added prose is load-bearing rationale rather than narration, and each line answers a question the next reader would otherwise ask of a test — why an id is a contract with the test layer so renaming one is a breaking change; why the dev-launcher handoff is empty on a release artifact and non-empty on a dev build; why the alarm mutation lives in the product rather than the harness; why a DOM-stub test may not claim an RN-published accessibility fact. A judgment pass over the added lines found no narration and no restated code to trim, so nothing was cut to buy a number. The largest riser, apps/mobile/vitest.projects.ts at 13.80% -> 46.80%, is a small file whose payload is now the explanation of why the two Vitest projects' include and exclude lists must stay exact complements: a file in both runs twice, a file in neither runs never, and vitest reports both as green. The other 18 are PRE-EXISTING RED ON origin/main and are absorbed rather than laundered — verified in a clean worktree at 3e555c8d, where this gate fails on these same files before any of this branch's commits. They are pinned at their current measured values so the branch is not red for something it did not cause, and the fact is recorded as an open observation in QUALITY.md so the absorption cannot be mistaken for a clean tree. No cap was widened, no allowlist entry was added, and every downward move --write found was taken first. Prior: #880. It also allowlists ten new files from the 15% CAP only (never from a pin): the seven RNTL scenario files, the testID vocabulary, the alarm mutation site and the RN device-seam registry. Each is a file whose prose is the payload — TESTING.md requires an RNTL case to state what cheaper layer cannot falsify it, an id vocabulary that does not say an id is a contract invites the rename that breaks the flows, and a mutation site with no argument for why it lives in the product is the first thing a later reader deletes. #892 hand-raises ONE pin and adds EIGHT allowlist entries. The pin is apps/web/tests/e2e/accessibility.spec.ts (13.33% -> 17.93%): the axe lane went from scanning one blueprint to all eight, and the added prose is the two sentences that say why eight and why the arrival assertion is not a heading match. The eight allowlist entries are new GATE files, and each carries its own reason above; they were trimmed first, not allowlisted first — doctor.ts 40.14 -> 27.55, golden-snapshot.ts 39.07 -> 28.54, golden-vault.test.ts 49.39 -> 35.36, accessibility.spec.ts 30.65 -> 17.93 — and what remains is the rationale that keeps each gate from being deleted by a future reader who cannot see what it catches. One further pin is raised that this change does NOT own, named rather than folded in: apps/mobile/src/apps/tally/TallyHome.test.tsx (31.21% -> 31.29%). #892 does not touch that file, and it measures the same drift against origin/main's own content — #890 changed it without re-pinning, so this gate has been red on main since c54367eb and blocks every PR that runs check:push. It is re-pinned to its MEASURED value (no content change, nothing hidden) because a pre-existing red that blocks everyone is precisely the 'nothing structural keeps main green' failure #892 exists to address. Attributed here so a reader does not mistake it for this change's regression. Two further #892 pins are raised for a purely ARITHMETIC reason, and it is the opposite of the usual one: apps/web/tests/e2e/web-pwa.spec.ts (11.14% -> 16.07%) has the SAME 384 comment characters it had before — not one was added — and apps/web/tests/e2e/accessibility.spec.ts FELL from 766 to 716. Both rose in SHARE because 48 lines of duplicated connected-session bootstrap left them for apps/web/tests/e2e/connect.ts, shrinking the denominator. SonarCloud flagged that duplication on this PR and the fix was extraction; trimming real prose to pay for it would be deleting rationale to buy back a number the extraction earned. This is the same denominator pathology QUALITY.md already records for this gate, running in the other direction. connect.ts itself is allowlisted from the 15% cap only, with its reason above.
